title: introduce-tenant-scoped-privilege-bundler-and-terraform-drift-detector-for-rbac-bootstrap
author: Aisha K. Raman
description:
Motivation: Private deployments require an auditable, least-privilege RBAC bootstrap that can be automatically generated from the actual infrastructure plan and Helm values used for install. This PR adds a tenant-scoped 'privilege bundler' that synthesizes minimal Role/ClusterRole and RoleBinding sets from live Terraform plans and chart values, plus a Terraform drift detector that fails bootstrap when plan drift would grant more privileges than intended.

What this change does (single string): adds a new cmd/installer subcommand (rbac-bundle) that ingests terraform plan JSON and Helm value snapshots, emits a policy bundle (k8s YAMLs) and a compact capability matrix (JSON) per-tenant; integrates a pre-apply drift check that compares generated policies against a stored allowlist and rejects bootstraps that expand capabilities unexpectedly; wires the bundler into the Private Installer post-apply hook so generated bundles are applied idempotently; provides a rollback runbook and a safe-retry mode which can automatically create a limited "bootstrap-sandbox" namespace for dry-run validation.

Key user-facing behavior: when operator runs private-installer with --rbac-auto, the installer will: 1) run terraform plan --out and convert tfplan to JSON, 2) compute minimal bindings per-tenant based on resource ownership annotations and Helm chart role templates, 3) run the drift detector against cluster state and stored allowlist, 4) apply generated bundle to a tenant-scoped namespace or fail fast with a clear remediation hint.

Implementation notes: the bundler uses a capability scoring heuristic (resource_kind, verbs, resource_name patterns) to compress allowed actions; policies are grouped into a bundle.yaml with deterministic ordering to keep diffs small; the drift detector uses a predicate engine that tolerates benign refactors (label changes) but flags verb/verb+resource expansions. The change adds unit/integration tests for the generator and drift detector and an operator E2E that validates idempotent apply/rollback.

Security and ops: KMS-wrapped signing was added so bundles are signed before applying (installer verifies signature). The PR also adds RBAC validation hooks so the installer will not bind a cluster-scoped role to a tenant namespace service account (prevents accidental cross-tenant escalation).

Checklist:
- [x] rbac-bundle generator CLI and Go library
- [x] terraform plan JSON adapter
- [x] drift detector and allowlist config format
- [x] post-apply hook integration and idempotent apply
- [x] bundle signing + verification (KMS integration in private builds)
- [x] runbook for rollback and safe-retry
- [x] unit + integration tests

Related: builds on design doc ENG-2481 (rbac bootstrap lifecycle) and the tenant-isolation audit in ENG-2623. Not intended to change defaults for existing installs unless operator opts into --rbac-auto.

Merge strategy: squash+merge to keep the bundler change as a single logical commit and simplify backporting.

review_conversation: Marco Li: Overall approach looks solid. Two concerns: (1) capability compression heuristic might under-approx in edge cases where wildcard patterns are used; we should provide an escape hatch. (2) need stronger unit tests for KMS signer error handling.
Aisha K. Raman: Added an explicit `--policy-escape` flag and documented it in the runbook; also added extra unit tests that simulate KMS failures (signing retry + clear error messages).

Priya Desai: Please ensure the installer does not ever auto-apply cluster-level bindings without explicit --allow-cluster-bindings. Also suggest we log the exact plan diff that's causing rejection to aid operators.

Aisha K. Raman: Added --allow-cluster-bindings flag gated behind an env var in private builds; drift detector now emits a compact plan diff artifact (stored in /var/log/redwood/rbac-diffs) and surfaces a truncated diff in CLI output.
Evan Thompson (security): What threat model did we use for signing? Do we rotate keys? How do we revoke a bundle?

Aisha K. Raman: Signed bundles include key id and timestamp; installer checks KMS key policy TTL. Revocation is via a denylist controller (separate follow-up ENG-2690) and the runbook includes steps to revoke and rollback an applied bundle. Added a TODO to link ENG-2690.
CI: initial run failed (lint error on pkg/rbac/bundler/heuristics.go: exported function without comment).
Aisha K. Raman: Fixed lint and re-ran CI; all checks green.
ci_checks: unit-tests: pass (pkg/rbac: 86% coverage on new code)
release_notes: Adds automated tenant-scoped RBAC bundle generator and terraform plan drift detector for Private installs. Operator opt-in via --rbac-auto. Includes bundle signing, idempotent apply, and rollback runbook.
